security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences or normal FastAPI example code. Confirmed risks include a remote installer piped to sh, public host binding, hardcoded secret and database defaults, permissive CORS, and unauthenticated user endpoints.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly into the shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace it with verified installation guidance that downloads, inspects, and pins the installer, or use trusted package manager instructions.

remediation.issue: Sample settings include hardcoded database and secret defaults.
remediation.suggestion: Make database URL and secret key required environment variables. Keep placeholders only in .env.example and never as runnable defaults.

remediation.issue: The guide shows permissive network and browser access defaults.
remediation.suggestion: Use explicit CORS origins, disable credentials unless required, and avoid 0.0.0.0 as a default development host.

remediation.issue: User management examples do not require authentication or authorization.
remediation.suggestion: Add current-user and permission dependencies before presenting list, read, create, or update user routes as production patterns.

semantic_findings.title: Permissive CORS Configuration
semantic_findings.description: The sample FastAPI app allows all origins, methods, headers, and credentials. If copied into production, authenticated browser requests can be exposed to unintended origins.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The CORS middleware configuration explicitly combines wildcard access with credentials. This is a common production security misconfiguration.

semantic_findings.title: Unauthenticated User Management Endpoints
semantic_findings.description: The sample user router lists, reads, creates, and updates users without an authentication or authorization dependency. If copied, it can allow user enumeration or unauthorized account changes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The route handlers depend only on the service dependency and show no current-user, role, or permission check. The endpoints operate on user records directly.

content.user_title: Build FastAPI APIs with uv and SQLAlchemy
content.value_statement: FastAPI projects often grow inconsistent when setup, config, database access, and tests are designed separately. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured FastAPI blueprint with uv, SQLAlchemy, Pydantic, Alembic, and pytest patterns.
actual_capabilities: Outlines a feature-based FastAPI project structure for Python services.
Provides uv setup commands for dependencies, development tools, and project initialization.
Shows Pydantic settings patterns for application, database, and security configuration.
Demonstrates async SQLAlchemy session setup, repositories, services, and models.
Includes Alembic migration guidance and pytest examples for API testing.
Lists common run, lint, format, type-check, and coverage commands.
limitations: It is a Markdown guidance skill, not a runnable FastAPI scaffold generator by itself.
Security-sensitive examples need review before production use.
Deployment, observability, and cloud infrastructure are not covered in depth.
Auth utilities are referenced but not fully implemented in the guide.

use_cases.title: Start a New API Service
use_cases.description: Create a consistent FastAPI project layout with uv, typed settings, database modules, tests, and common development commands.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Patterns
use_cases.description: Align routes, services, repositories, schemas, migrations, and tests across multiple Python API contributors.

use_cases.title: Upgrade an Existing FastAPI App
use_cases.description: Refactor an existing service toward async SQLAlchemy, modular feature folders, Pydantic v2 settings, and pytest coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Project Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this FastAPI skill to plan a new Python API project with uv, SQLAlchemy, Pydantic settings, Alembic, and pytest. Include the folder structure and first setup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Feature Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this FastAPI skill to design a products feature module. Include schemas, model fields, repository methods, service methods, routes, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Existing App
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this FastAPI skill to review my app structure. Identify gaps in configuration, database sessions, migrations, repositories, services, routes, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this FastAPI skill to prepare a production readiness checklist for my service. Cover settings, database migrations, CORS, auth boundaries, tests, linting, and deployment commands.

output_examples.input: Plan a new customer API using FastAPI and uv.
output: A domain-based folder map for the customer feature.
A setup sequence for uv, dependencies, tests, linting, and migrations.
A short list of configuration and security decisions to confirm before implementation.

output_examples.input: Add database access patterns for a user module.
output: A repository and service design using async SQLAlchemy sessions.
Pydantic request and response schema guidance.
Test scenarios for create, read, update, and duplicate-email behavior.

output_examples.input: Review my FastAPI project for missing structure.
output: A concise gap list covering settings, routers, models, migrations, tests, and tooling.
Prioritized next steps for aligning the project with the skill patterns.

best_practices: Require production secrets through environment variables or a managed secret store.
Keep feature folders cohesive, with routes, schemas, services, repositories, and tests together.
Run migrations, tests, linting, formatting, and type checks before release.
anti_patterns: Do not copy placeholder secrets or database passwords into production code.
Do not expose development servers on all network interfaces without a clear need.
Do not publish user management routes without authentication and authorization checks.

faq.question: Does this skill create a complete FastAPI project automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that Claude, Codex, or Claude Code can use while helping you create files.

faq.question: Which Python version does the guide target?
faq.answer: It targets Python 3.12 or newer and modern FastAPI, Pydantic v2, SQLAlchemy 2.0, and pytest patterns.

faq.question: Does it include database migrations?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Alembic setup guidance and an async migration environment pattern.

faq.question: Can I use SQLite with this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The guide mentions SQLite for development and in-memory SQLite for tests, while PostgreSQL is the main database target.

faq.question: Does it implement authentication completely?
faq.answer: No. It references authentication modules and security helpers, but full authentication implementation must be added separately.

faq.question: Is the guidance production ready as written?
faq.answer: No. Review secrets, CORS, host binding, authentication, deployment, and operational settings before production use.
